gen_risks.description: High insecurity and ongoing conflict in target regions may restrict access to project locations, disrupt service delivery, and hinder direct field supervision.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt adaptive implementation modalities, including remote monitoring via GEMS, third-party monitoring, remote delivery channels, and partnerships with local CBOs and NGOs.
gen_risks.evidence: high insecurity in some of the areas in which project activities will be conducted

gen_risks.description: Targeting vulnerable populations in fragile settings creates a heightened risk of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH).
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement an SEA/SH Action Plan, enforce strict codes of conduct, recruit a dedicated GBV/SEA/SH specialist, and set up a sensitive grievance mechanism with referral pathways.
gen_risks.evidence: SEA/SH risk is Substantial, reflecting the nature of project activities and the vulnerability of the target population

gen_risks.description: The implementing ministry currently lacks a functional PIU with established financial management systems, software, and World Bank project experience.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit qualified financial management specialists before effectiveness, acquire approved accounting software, prepare a financial procedures manual, and establish internal audit oversight.
gen_risks.evidence: The assessment found that the MFS currently does not have a PIU with FM arrangements in place

gen_risks.description: Public administrative routines and multi-layered approval processes may cause significant procurement delays and impede implementation timelines.
gen_risks.mitigation: Define maximum review and approval delays per procurement stage in the Project Implementation Manual and provide dedicated training to bid committees.
gen_risks.evidence: administrative routines may result in procurement delays, potentially affecting project implementation

gen_risks.description: Procurement in fragile or insecure zones with limited active suppliers risks restricting market competition, inflating prices, and increasing collusion risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply flexible World Bank procurement procedures tailored for fragile situations and phase activity launches starting in accessible communes.
gen_risks.evidence: procurement in fragile areas with few bidders can restrict competition and possibly increase prices and collusion risks

gen_risks.description: Insufficient technical capacity within the PIU and bid committees may result in weak contract administration and poor oversight of major procurement contracts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit an experienced full-time procurement specialist, establish formal contract management plans in STEP, and conduct capacity-building workshops.
gen_risks.evidence: insufficient capacity can lead to poor contract management and administration of big contracts

gen_risks.description: Civil works for constructing 28 warehouses and rehabilitating 10 regional centers could cause soil and water pollution and worker safety hazards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Screen subprojects using E&S procedures, prepare site-specific ESIAs/ESMPs, and mandate compliance with occupational health and safety standards.
gen_risks.evidence: key E&S risks and impacts include water and soil pollution from solid and liquid waste at construction and rehabilitation sites

gen_risks.description: Connecting the Unique Social Registry with national ID and payment systems creates data privacy and cybersecurity vulnerabilities regarding beneficiary data.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce national data protection laws under CIL oversight and adopt security and data-exchange protocols approved by the National Cybersecurity Agency (ANSSI).
gen_risks.evidence: follow the security procedures elaborated by the National Cybersecurity Agency (ANSSI)

gen_risks.description: The fluid national political environment in Burkina Faso may cause institutional shifts, policy changes, or governance bottlenecks during project execution.
gen_risks.mitigation: Anchor project activities within the broader national PAMPV strategy and utilize the multi-sectoral Steering Committee to maintain institutional alignment.
gen_risks.evidence: the country's current fluid political situation.

gen_risks.description: Severe fragmentation across social protection actors and ministries risks creating coordination bottlenecks, operational overlap, and communication failures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a functional inter-ministerial Steering Committee and formalize operational protocols and data-sharing frameworks across participating institutions.
gen_risks.evidence: Burkina Faso’s social assistance system is highly fragmented, with more than 200 interventions implemented by 50 agencies.

gen_risks.description: Flaws in targeting or social barriers could lead to the exclusion of marginalized groups, such as IDPs, women, youth, and persons with disabilities, from economic benefits.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize RSU proxy means testing combined with community validation assemblies, enforce gender quotas, and deploy an accessible Grievance Redress Mechanism.
gen_risks.evidence: exclusion from the project’s benefits of certain categories of people such as vulnerable groups including women, youth, people with disabilities

gen_risks.description: Land acquisition or site clearing for warehouse construction and provincial intake center upgrades could result in localized economic displacement.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prioritize available public land, screen all construction sites for resettlement impacts, and formulate Resettlement Action Plans or Livelihood Restoration Plans as needed.
gen_risks.evidence: ESS 5: Land Acquisition, Restrictions on Land Use and Involuntary Resettlement... economic displacement.

gen_risks.description: Delays in fulfilling post-effectiveness legal covenants, such as recruiting mandatory key specialists, could slow down overall project initiation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Initiate recruitment processes early during preparation and closely track legal covenant compliance deadlines post-effectiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: The PIU shall include the following additional key staff... no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk is assessed to be Substantial. The uncertain political and governance context provides a challenge to long-term development policy. Adaptive social protection systems are still nascent and will require continued political commitment.
gt_risks.mitigation: The team, guided by the management, will continue its high-level policy dialogue at central and decentralized levels and ensure continuous advocacy and communication.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is assessed to be Substantial. Fiscal space remains constrained by elevated security spending and tighter financing conditions, which increase the risk of reduced budget allocations and delayed counterpart funding for new priorities and reforms, including social protection and the PAMPV. Macroeconomic risks also arise from exogenous factors, including current conflict in the Middle East which can result in a surge in oil prices and put inflationary pressure.
gt_risks.mitigation: Other programs such as the International Monetary Fund program and the World Bank's technical assistance on tax expenditure under the Sustainable Development Finance Policy can help expand fiscal space, partially mitigating these risks.

gt_risks.description: Sector strategy and policies risks are considered to be Substantial. Sectoral strategies and policies remain nascent, and the Government's budget allocation to operationalize the PAMPV remains unclear. Also, sectoral decisions are at times taken abruptly and can heavily affect implementation (for example, the suspension of cash transfers in 2023 led to an increased focus on economic inclusion, and the newly emerged priority of the CONASUR/IDPs led to the revision of the fiche de projet of this project).
gt_risks.mitigation: In parallel with high-level policy dialogue, the project supports strategic communications, adopts an agile approach, and provides technical assistance to promote evidence-based decision-making (with support from SASPP, the Social Protection Response MDTF, and the State and Peacebuilding Fund).

gt_risks.description: Overall fiduciary risks are considered as Substantial, as described in section IV.B and annex 2, based on financial assessment and procurement assessment.
gt_risks.mitigation: The project preparation fund (Grant Facility for Project Preparation) has been used not only to prepare mitigation measures to address these risks but will also elevate the project readiness (for example, effectiveness-linked actions including FM and procurement staffing and initiating the procurement packages for the first 18-months' implementation priorities) to improve the project performance.

gt_risks.description: Other risks related to insecurity are rated as High. The deteriorating and volatile security situation—particularly in regions with high poverty, displacement, and food insecurity that are project intervention areas—will likely be an important risk. The project will also address other risks related to protection of personal data: for Component 2 on social registry and interoperability, activities will be guided by the Information System Security Policy (ISSP) document developed by the ANSSI, to ensure confidentiality of households registered in the RSU.
gt_risks.mitigation: The project activities will be adjusted based on the security situation (see annex 3), and the PIU will be also staffed with a security specialist and a security management plan will be developed. To remain engaged, the project will also rely on remote delivery/monitoring, partnering with local representation (NGOs, UN agencies). The ST-RSU will conduct capacity-building activities, including training sessions and awareness campaigns, to strengthen users' ability to manage and protect households' personal data.
